reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays and adds shared predicates (skipsWeekendOccurrences, isNonWorkingDay), but no shared 'skip, move or keep this occurrence' function, so every consumer composes them itself.

duplication.why: The skip-vs-move-vs-keep decision is re-written in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and schedule-template's getMovedDate, and getUpcomingDates/getDatesInRange repeat the same occurrences->filter->adjust->dayFromDate pipeline with two different lookahead heuristics (getDailyWeekdayLookahead vs getWeekendShiftDays).

placement.why: Date rules sit in shared/schedules.ts as the tree does, but getWeekendShiftDays lives in schedules/app.ts and shared/schedules.ts now imports a server RSchedule type.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedule date computation, the new handler and the RecurConfig type, with tests.

maintainability.why: Each new weekend rule (daily skip, holidays, yearly holidays) must be remembered at four call sites with slightly different shapes, inviting drift between upcoming dates, next date, ranges and budget templates.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange (schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (budget/schedule-template.ts) each decide skip/move themselves via skipsWeekendOccurrences + getDateWithSkippedWeekend instead of one shared occurrence-adjustment function like the logic inside getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: The skip/move decision appears as an early-return branch in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates, a filter+ternary in getDatesInRange and a `skipWeekend && !skipsWeekendDays` ternary in schedule-template; the lookahead bound is computed twice under different names.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays and RSchedule data gains frequency/holidays; getNextDate gets a daily-skip special branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template re-implement the skip-or-move choice.
